title: Fine-Tuning Language Models Using Formal Methods Feedback: A Use Case in Autonomous Systems
problem: Language models deployed in autonomous systems may violate formal safety specifications or exhibit behaviors inconsistent with required properties. Fine-tuning mechanisms that incorporate formal verification feedback are needed to align model outputs with formal requirements.
motivation: Autonomous systems require provable safety and correctness guarantees, making it essential to ensure language models behave according to formal specifications.
method: The approach uses formal verification (checking whether outputs satisfy strict logical safety specifications through techniques like model checking or theorem proving) to evaluate the model's behavior. When violations are detected, the verification produces training signals. The model then learns from them by adjusting its parameters (through gradient-based optimization) to minimize error signals derived from specification violations—teaching it to consistently follow the formal safety requirements.
key_novelty: The key innovation is integrating formal verification feedback directly into the fine-tuning process, so the model learns to produce outputs that satisfy formal safety specifications.
contributions: A framework for incorporating formal verification feedback into LLM fine-tuning
Demonstration that formal feedback improves specification compliance in model outputs
Evaluation on autonomous systems use cases showing reduced formal property violations
Method for translating formal specifications into fine-tuning training signals
limitations: Computational overhead of formal verification, scalability to larger models, and generalization to diverse autonomous systems domains are not discussed.
primary_theme: Formal methods-guided LLM fine-tuning for autonomous systems
